title: Inspect a design without losing its history
statement: As a developer, I can focus a named whiteboard and reopen an exact revision so I can inspect a design in the context in which it was authored.
overview:
A named board is an independent document built with the shared diagram grammar. Sections give a large design local reading context, while explicit connections explain how areas relate. A reader can pan, zoom and focus without replacing the document with an unrelated diagram.

Publication appends a complete immutable revision and requires the observed parent. This code-derived story remains proposed; implementation evidence is not a product acceptance decision.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Publishing one named whiteboard leaves the current revisions of other named whiteboards unchanged.
acceptance_criteria.title: Independent documents
acceptance_criteria.overview: ERD, Infrastructure and Data flows are document conventions rather than separate diagram engines.

acceptance_criteria.statement: An exact whiteboard revision remains readable after a newer revision is published.
acceptance_criteria.title: Exact historical view
acceptance_criteria.overview: Source pins remain those of the selected revision; a reader must not silently adopt a newer entity definition.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A publication that names an outdated parent is rejected instead of overwriting the current board.
acceptance_criteria.title: Concurrent update guard
acceptance_criteria.overview: The author rereads the current revision and makes an explicit update.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A reader can focus a section or element by its instance path within the named whiteboard.
acceptance_criteria.title: Section focus
acceptance_criteria.overview: Repeated appearances retain distinct paths even when they refer to the same source identity.
